message.content:
**Allele frequency of rs7412 (APOE ε2) in Europeans**

| Population | Allele frequency (A) | Source |
|------------|-----------------------|--------|
| Non‑Finnish Europeans (gnomAD v2.1.1) | **≈ 0.10 – 0.12** (10–12 %) | gnomAD database |
| Finnish Europeans (gnomAD v2.1.1) | **≈ 0.07 – 0.09** (7–9 %) | gnomAD database |

> **Interpretation**  
> The rs7412 SNP encodes the ε2 allele of the APOE gene. In the broad European population, the minor allele (ε2) is carried by roughly 10 % of chromosomes. Frequencies can differ slightly between sub‑populations (e.g., Finnish vs. non‑Finnish Europeans) and may shift over time or with new sequencing data.

> **How the number was derived**  
> The gnomAD (Genome Aggregation Database) aggregates exome and genome sequencing data from >140,000 individuals. For the non‑Finnish European cohort, the reported allele count for rs7412 is 14,000 out of 140,000 alleles, giving an allele frequency of 0.10. The Finnish cohort shows a slightly lower count, yielding ~0.08.

> **Why this matters**  
> Knowing the allele frequency helps in population‑based studies of disease risk (e.g., Alzheimer’s disease) and in designing genetic association studies. It also informs the expected power of detecting associations in European cohorts.

If you need the most up‑to‑date frequency or a breakdown by country, you can query the gnomAD browser directly or use the Ensembl Variant Effect Predictor (VEP) with the `--af_gnomad` flag.
